PullRequest.Title: [1.147] agentHost: wait for a spawned subagent's recorded agent instead of sleeping 10 ms
PullRequest.Body:
Cherry-pick of #348682 to `release/1.147`, a test-only fix for the flake `AH-AGENTSERVICE-PERSIST-SLEEP-10` that failed release/1.147 pipeline 727 run [497609](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=497609) on Windows.

Two `AgentService - chats with their own agent` tests slept 10 ms before reading a subagent's agent, which the host records in the background through an asynchronous database write. They now wait for that record, with a 5 s bound. The details and the proof are on #348682. The test file was identical on both branches, so this is a clean `cherry-pick -x`. `agentServiceChatProviders.test.ts` passes 39 of 39 on this branch.

For the endgame champ to decide whether it goes into 1.147. It changes no product code.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Spawn a subagent under a chat using a different agent, then assert its persisted provider and routing (test-only change).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test now awaits the existing private-chat insertion completing, which follows the existing provider-record write, instead of sleeping 10 ms. Production spawn handling remains asynchronous and unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the session catalog to check legacy private-chat storage handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing catalog-snapshot request per spawn; a legacy-only state write is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same spawn event issued the same catalog request before the fixed sleep.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains background work from the production spawn handler; not newly awaited by the helper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the subagent provider, read its session catalog, then insert the private-chat row through insertPrivateChatV2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider write and one successful insertion for the single new subagent, plus the existing catalog snapshot; existing conflict retries are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical writes and snapshots were scheduled, but assertions ran after an unconditional 10 ms delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already background production work; its completion now gates test assertions rather than a timer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted chat-agent providers and select the subagent record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One explicit database read, unchanged; the get operation merely moves into the preceding assignment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One identical read after timeout(10), followed by the same map lookup in the assertion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One spawned subagent in each of two tests, each with a fresh service and in-memory catalog database; no changed collection-sized loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One helper invocation per fresh database. Existing peer-catalog writes serialize per session, and private insertions use the existing database transaction sequencer. The wrapper forwards each insertion exactly once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing service caches the provider-map load and updates it on writes; failed loads clear the cached promise. The test still performs one explicit provider-map read. The new helper neither polls nor adds cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff only adds a test-local promise wrapper and replaces two sleeps; the wrapper awaits and forwards the original insertion without retrying.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Database completion time varies by test environment; no additional database calls or scalable production work are introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added allocation and wrapper are constant-sized and scoped to disposable, per-test databases; production behavior is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Delete a parent chat and verify persisted agent records for it and its subagent are removed (test-only synchronization change).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test now completes the pre-existing spawn persistence before reading the initial records and invoking disposeChat. Deletion already waits for outstanding session catalog writes before removing membership and provider records.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the spawned chat using the same provider-write/catalog-read/private-insertion chain as the routing test, then read provider keys before and after deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One spawned chat's persistence and two explicit provider-map reads, identical to the previous successful scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations ran, with a 10 ms sleep used to assume spawn persistence had finished.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence now gates the initial read deterministically; the two explicit reads remain awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove catalog membership, delete parent/descendant provider metadata in a batched request, and persist the remaining session catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parent deletion; both provider identities fit in one existing SQL deletion batch. Other deletion/state operations are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical deletion path, batching, and persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited by disposeChat, including waiting for prior peer-store writes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clean up chat data through the existing test-configured services; the fixture uses an in-memory file service and mock agents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same parent and single descendant as before; no changed filesystem or subprocess fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deletion invoked the same ancillary cleanup through the same fixture services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited cleanup remains on deletion's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One parent chat and one subagent in a fresh test database. Provider deletion receives the two identities together, not a new per-descendant request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One spawn followed by one awaited parent deletion; existing session mutation and peer-store queues preserve serialization. The diff adds no parallel work or new worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing provider-map cache is updated on recording and deletion. The test's two explicit before/after reads remain unchanged, and the helper is not shared with subsequent tests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed test retains one spawn, one deletion, and two provider reads; the helper installs only one wrapper on its per-test database, which is disposed during teardown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured timing is available; deletion costs and input sizes are unchanged, and the new wait only observes an existing write.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression or cross-test retention. This is a synchronization change, not added cleanup work or boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the entire single-file inventory and all four diff hunks for performance-review, tracing spawn persistence, provider-cache behavior, per-test ownership, database serialization, and deletion batching. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or shipped performance regression fix found.
